findings.title: remove_member uses group.users.delete, skipping GroupUser destroy callbacks
findings.body:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through deletes the GroupUser join row with a raw `delete_all`, so GroupUser `after_destroy` callbacks do not run. In Discourse those callbacks (`remove_primary_group`, `remove_title`) clear the user's `primary_group_id` and group-derived title. After removal through this endpoint, the user can still have the removed group as their primary group and keep its title, leaving stale data.

The previous code called `group.remove(user)`, which destroys the GroupUser records and fires the callbacks. Use that here instead. The trailing `group.save` also does nothing, because the delete has already been persisted.

findings.title: Adding a username that is already a member raises and 500s, leaving a partial add
findings.body:
`group.add(user)` is `users.push(user)`, which immediately inserts a GroupUser row, and nothing checks for existing membership first. If the admin enters a username that is already in the group, the unique (group_id, user_id) constraint raises `RecordNotUnique` and the request returns a 500.

Usernames processed before the duplicate have already been committed, so the add is partial. On the client, `Group#addMembers` has no error handler, so the admin gets no feedback and the list is not refreshed.

The old UI sent the full usernames list through `usernames=`, which diffed membership, so this case did not arise. Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`.

findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50), this gives 2 instead of 1. The pager then shows "1/2" with Next enabled. Clicking Next sets offset to 50 (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), the server returns an empty page, and the admin sees "2/2" with no members. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Removed PATCH/nested-param API now silently resets visibility for existing callers
findings.body:
The incremental `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add:, delete:}` and the nested `group: {...}` params for PUT and POST have been removed, but the routes still accept these requests.

A PATCH from an existing API client now reaches `update`, which does no membership change. Because `params[:visible]` is absent, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` sets the group to invisible and returns success. Clients still sending `group[visible]`/`group[name]` to PUT get the same silent visibility reset.

POST `/admin/groups` with `group[name]` now creates nothing and returns a validation error, because `params[:name]` is nil.

Either keep backward compatibility for these callers, or only assign `visible` when the parameter is present.

findings.title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no pagination
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` now always applies `limit` (default 50), and `findMembers` requests only the first page. The public `group/members.hbs` template iterates `members` but has no next/previous controls, unlike the admin template. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. Any group with more than 50 members now silently shows a truncated list on the public group page, and users have no way to see the rest.

findings.title: Public /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from array to object
findings.body: The endpoint previously returned a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. Any external API consumer, or other client code still treating the response as an array, will break. No spec was added or updated in `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` to cover the new shape or the pagination meta.

findings.title: members limit/offset are unvalidated (no cap, negatives cause 500)
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` are taken directly from params. Anyone who can see a group can pass a very large `limit` (e.g. on trust_level_0 or everyone-sized groups) and force serialization of every member in one request. A negative `limit` or `offset` makes PostgreSQL raise and the request returns a 500. A `limit` of 0 is echoed back in `meta.limit` and causes a division by zero in the client pager. Clamp `limit` to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and `offset` to at least 0.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE
findings.body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but `config/routes.rb` maps `remove_member` only to `DELETE members`. Controller specs dispatch straight to the action without checking the HTTP verb, so the test passes while exercising a request shape the app never routes. Use `:delete` to match the real route.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember have no failure handling
findings.body: Both `addMembers` and `removeMember` only chain a success callback. The controller actions only chain onto these promises (for `addMembers` the promise is not even returned). When the server responds with an error, the UI shows nothing to the admin: for example, the 422 for automatic groups, or a 500 on duplicate member insert. The failure is silent and the admin cannot tell whether the change was applied. The input is also never cleared after a successful add, as the TODO acknowledges.
